title: Every object attracts every other object
summary: Newton's law of gravitation, as OpenStax states it, says every object attracts every other object.
body: OpenStax Physics says the gravitational force is always attractive and depends only on the masses and the distance. In the book's wording of the universal law, every object in the universe attracts every other object, along the line joining them. The force grows with the product of the masses and shrinks with the square of the distance. The book gives a measured value of the gravitational constant in that section. Urone and Hinrichs, 26 March 2020. A standards-table value of that constant is a different card.

sources.title: 7.2 Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation
sources.author: Paul Peter Urone and Roger Hinrichs
sources.note: Paraphrase only, not a quotation. OpenStax Physics, Paul Peter Urone and Roger Hinrichs, published 26 March 2020. The assigned licence for /books/physics/ is CC BY 4.0; the page footer also prints a noncommercial clause, so this card does not copy the sentence. Supports the statement that every object attracts every other, proportional to the masses and inversely to the square of the distance.
